text:
Alex Ovechkin is 41, in his 22nd NHL season, and his job has changed. He's playing under 14 minutes a night and has 1 goal in 15 games, added to the 929 he brought into the season, already past Wayne Gretzky's old record.

The shooting is the story, and our numbers read it as a cold spell rather than an ending. He has 1 goal on 4.7 expected goals (a measure of the quality of his chances). He's gone ten games without scoring, but on 3.6 expected goals in that stretch, more than his usual rate. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 94th percentile last season for chances from the home-plate area in front of the net, and his top shot speed this season still ranks in the 97th percentile. What's gone is the skating: his top speed sits at the very bottom of the NHL EDGE tracking.

Off the ice, the week's headlines were about "Ovi's Office" to young cancer patients at the Capitals' Hockey Fights Cancer skate (NHL.com). On it, watch the power play: he has no power-play points yet, and when the one-timer starts landing there, the goals should follow.
headline: Ovechkin at 41: the looks are still there
